not_covered.text: Three Palestinians are reportedly killed in Gaza City, bringing the total casualties to 7 in the past 24 hours.
A Board of Peace official reports that Hamas will disarm its weapons in the coming days.
The Bermuda-flagged LNG tanker Gaslog Shanghai, which was carrying LNG oil from Qatar, is reported to have been among the two vessels hit yesterday in the Strait of Hormuz.
A tanker near Oman is hit by an unknown projectile.
The Houthis in Yemen deny reports of imposing tolls on vessels passing through the Bab-el-Mandeb strait.
The Washington Post reports that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu blocked a request by former U.S. Senator Lindsey Graham to transfer an Iron Dome system from the U.S. to Ukraine.

Ukrainian forces sink a Rosatom-owned container ship in the Black Sea, forcing its 17-member crew to abandon it. Rosatom says it had been transporting civilian goods, including frozen food and construction materials.

Sudan and Egypt reaches an agreement on a 16-month plan to rehabilitate the Jebel Aulia Dam south of Khartoum, Sudan, including the construction of a temporary bridge, after the dam was damaged in November 2023 during shelling by the Rapid

not_covered.text: A truck bomb explodes beside a police station in Cúcuta, Norte de Santander, Colombia, injuring eight police officers and three civilians.
At least three people are killed and 15 others are injured in an explosion at a coffeehouse in Moscow, Russia.

The U.S. FBI opens an investigation after the U.S. state of Michigan reports a cyberattack on its water systems, including whether Iran was behind the cyberattack, a day after Minnesota reported a similar breach.
